findings.summary: The scope list items "Ranking", "Indexing", "JS-heavy rendering", "Login-walled pages" appear as bare lines with no label saying they are out of scope.
findings.evidence:
"Example system: a Google-style Web Crawler
Ranking
Indexing
JS-heavy rendering
Login-walled pages"
findings.fix: Add an explicit 'Out of scope:' header above these four items so a skimmer does not read them as in-scope features.

findings.summary: The delay bullet packs three rules into one line, and the 'max(1s, 10x last fetch time)' formula conflicts with the later 'Delay' wording in the cheatsheet ('1 request/sec per host, or 10x last fetch time').
findings.evidence: "Delay = max(1s, 10x last fetch time), or the host's Crawl-delay if larger" vs. cheatsheet "Politeness: 1 request/sec per host, or 10x last fetch time"
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets (base delay, 10x rule, Crawl-delay override), and state the cheatsheet as 'max(1s, 10x last fetch time)' to match.

findings.summary: The sample robots.txt sets Crawl-delay: 5, but the page never states how it interacts with the 1s/10x rule, and the 'Crawl-delay if larger' wording is the only hint.
findings.evidence: "Crawl-delay: 5" in the code block, with no worked result next to the delay examples
findings.fix: Add one line: 'Crawl-delay 5 and a 200 ms fetch → wait 5s (the larger value)'.

findings.summary: The failure table is followed by three bare negative statements that restate defenses as problems without labels, so they read as extra unlabeled rules.
findings.evidence:
"Strict parser that raises on bad HTML stalls the pool
Trusting the HTTP charset header alone garbles text and links
Parsing without a size cap lets one page exhaust worker memory"
findings.fix: Put them under a 'Mistakes to avoid' header or fold them into the table's Problem column.

findings.summary: The exact store is described as having no false positives, but a 64-bit URL hash can collide.
findings.evidence: Exact store: sharded KV keyed by the 64-bit URL hash ... Precise: no false positives, no false negatives
findings.fix: Say 'effectively no false positives (a 64-bit hash collides with probability ~1e-9 per pair at 10B URLs, so a few collisions are expected), or store the full URL/longer hash to confirm a hit'.

findings.summary: The Bloom filter false-positive is described inconsistently: the first section says a wrong 'seen' loses a page, while the Bloom+KV column says the error cost is none, and the comparison puts Bloom-alone 'Cost of error' as 'new URL dropped' without saying that this only applies to Bloom alone.
findings.evidence: "A wrong "seen" answer loses a page" and "Bloom first, KV on hit" vs. table "Errors | 1% false positives | none | none"
findings.fix: Label the Bloom column as 'Bloom alone' and add a note that the KV confirmation removes the false-positive loss.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "alternative", "similarity").
findings.evidence: Alternative: MinHash with shingles estimates Jaccard similarity; better for set overlap, heavier than SimHash
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: MinHash is explained with the terms "shingles" and "Jaccard", and neither is defined for the learner.
findings.evidence: MinHash column: "estimates Jaccard on shingles" and "heavier; best for set overlap"
findings.fix: Add one line before the table: a shingle is a short run of consecutive words, and Jaccard similarity is the overlap of two shingle sets divided by their union.

findings.summary: The recrawl outcome flow repeats each outcome node as both a branch and a source, making the diagram hard to follow, and the 304 ratio bullet holds two opposite interpretations in one line.
findings.evidence: "304 ratio: high means cheap checks work, or intervals are too short"
findings.fix: Draw the flow as a single decision with two terminal branches that both go to 'Clamp to 1h..30d, set next_crawl', and split the 304 bullet into two.

findings.summary: The 'Adding a Node' section holds the 9% example as a bare number without the arithmetic, and the 1/N rule is stated as 'only ~1/N of hosts move' while the example (10 to 11 nodes) is 1/11.
findings.evidence: "Example: 10 nodes to 11 moves about 9% of hosts"
findings.fix: Write '10 → 11 nodes: 1/11 ≈ 9% of hosts move' so the number can be checked.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "correctness", "threshold").
findings.evidence: Trade-off: exact versus Bloom dedup (memory vs correctness) and SimHash threshold (recall vs false merges)
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The trade-offs table lists 'Bloom filter ... Drops ~1% of new URLs' without noting that the design on page 7 pairs Bloom with a KV store to avoid exactly this.
findings.evidence: "Bloom filter | ~12 GB at 1% FP | Drops ~1% of new URLs"
findings.fix: Change to 'Bloom alone' and add a row or note: 'Bloom + KV on hit removes the drops at the cost of a KV read per hit'.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "conditional", "adaptive").
findings.evidence: Recrawl: adaptive interval 1h-30d, conditional GET, tiers by change rate
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.
